title: Long-tail promptset hedging and asymmetric rollback rules for Optimize
creator: Leah Martinez
description: PRD: Define a compact, production-ready spec for handling regressions driven by long-tail prompt coverage. The goal is a hedging strategy and asymmetric rollback rules that reduce noisy stops while protecting customer-facing quality. This ticket captures acceptance criteria, signal definitions, A/B test rules, and automated rollback triggers for Optimize eval pipelines.
background: We ship model changes and quantization profiles frequently. Standard symmetric thresholds often overreact to rare long-tail prompts and cause unnecessary rollbacks. Teams have requested a principled way to: 1) protect high-severity cohorts (e.g., safety, billing), 2) tolerate minor noise on low-usage tails, and 3) automate safe rollback for clear degradations. This spec balances sensitivity and operational noise using cohort-weighted deltas and asymmetric rules (stricter on hallucination/accuracy, looser on latency/cost within bounds).
goals: Protect high-severity cohorts with low false-negative risk
Reduce rollback churn caused by rare prompt spikes
Enable automated rollback for unambiguous quality regressions
Provide clear A/B acceptance criteria for canary runs
non_goals: Replace human review for ambiguous regressions
Design new evaluation tooling—this builds on existing Optimize pipelines
Handle non-text modalities in this ticket
proposal_summary: Introduce a three-tier cohort classification (Core, Sensitive, Long-tail), compute weighted composite deltas per rollout, apply asymmetric thresholds per signal type (quality/hallucination stricter than latency), and add an early-warning mechanism that quarantines canaries for manual review if borderline. Implement automated rollback when weighted composite delta exceeds defined high-confidence thresholds for Sensitive or Core cohorts, or when multiple independent high-priority signals cross thresholds simultaneously.
promptset_strategy: 1) Maintain canonical Core promptset (top 90% by usage) and Sensitive promptset (security, billing, safety examples). 2) Long-tail promptset sampled continuously from production logs via reservoir sampling with TTLed snapshots. 3) Use stratified sampling during canaries: 70% Core, 20% Sensitive, 10% Long-tail. 4) Always include deterministic seed examples for run-to-run comparability.
eval_design: A/B canary with 5% traffic ramp over 24 hours. Metrics computed hourly. Use bootstrapped confidence intervals and direction-aware deltas. Composite delta = 0.6 * quality_delta + 0.3 * hallucination_delta + 0.1 * latency_penalty. For Long-tail, apply a smoothing window and minimum sample count to avoid overreacting to single outliers.
metrics_and_thresholds: quality_delta (positive is worse): Core > 1.5% -> actionable; Sensitive > 1.0% -> immediate rollback; Long-tail > 5% -> flag for review
hallucination_rate increase: Sensitive > 0.5% absolute -> immediate rollback; Core > 1.0% absolute -> rollback
latency_p50 increase: if p50 increases > 40% but p95 <= 25% -> investigate but do not auto-rollback
composite_weighted_delta: Sensitive >= 1.2 -> auto-rollback; Core >= 1.5 -> auto-rollback; Long-tail >= 3.0 -> quarantine (manual review)
minimum sample counts: Core >= 2000 samples per hourly window, Sensitive >= 200, Long-tail >= 50; below minimum, mark signal as low-confidence
ab_criteria: Canary must maintain composite_delta within thresholds for two consecutive 4-hour windows before ramping from 5% to 25%
Statistical test: use two-sided bootstrap with 95% CI; if CI excludes zero in the harmful direction and meets threshold, count as failed
Stop early if multiple independent signals (quality, hallucination) exceed their respective sensitive thresholds in a single window
rollback_triggers: Immediate rollback triggers: Sensitive hallucination delta > 0.5% absolute in an hourly window
High-confidence composite trigger: composite_weighted_delta >= sensitive auto-rollback threshold with sample counts satisfied
Multi-signal trigger: two or more signals (quality_delta, hallucination_rate, regression of key rollout KPIs) exceed medium thresholds concurrently
Safety-critical customer impact (manually reported or Slack alert with P0 label) -> stop-the-line rollback
monitoring_signals: per-example worst-case deltas (top 50 regressions) with links to traces
token-level hallucination alerts aggregated by endpoint and model-version
customer-facing error or abuse reports tagged to model version
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Internal dry-run on a replay dataset (no traffic)
Stage 1: Canary 5% traffic (24h) with automated monitoring and quarantine rules
Stage 2: Conditional ramp to 25% if two consecutive windows are green
Stage 3: Full ramp after 72h of stable metrics or manual approval
success_criteria: Reduction in false-positive rollbacks by >= 30% over 90 days
No customer-facing hallucination incidents attributable to canaries during rollout windows
Stable composite_delta distribution for Core prompts across 4 consecutive rollouts
dependencies: ENG-21355 (alerting): new quarantine alert types and auto-rollback hook
DES-1199: visualizations for per-cohort composite deltas in Console
